name: Kybella for neck/jowl

lead: Kybella is the brand name of deoxycholic acid, an injectable the US FDA approved on April 29, 2015 for reducing moderate-to-severe fat below the chin. People after a sharper jawline or neck also discuss it for the jowl area, which is not part of the approved indication.

When injected into submental fat it destroys fat cells, which the body then metabolizes over several months. A generic version became available in the US in April 2021, and a 2025 registered study examined patient satisfaction with combined face and neck treatments including Kybella.

paras: It is a clinic treatment given by a clinician as a series of injections into the fat under the chin, with the reduction showing over the following months. It is sold as Belkyra in some markets such as Australia.

Treatment is clinician-administered and prescription-only. The source reviewed does not detail adverse effects, so patients are referred to the product label and their clinician for the risk profile. Jowl and other neck uses are off-label.

angle.text: Kybella injections destroy fat cells under the chin for a slimmer chin and neck, with the reduction visible after treatment. The FDA approved it in 2015 for submental fat; jowl and neck use is off-label.

lead: Kybella is a prescription injection of deoxycholic acid, a bile acid that dissolves fat cells where it is injected. It is approved in the US to improve the appearance of moderate-to-severe fullness under the chin ('submental fat'), and people use it to slim the double-chin area and sharpen the line between chin and neck. [1][1]

Looksmaxxing and aesthetic discussion extends the idea to the jowls and other parts of the lower face and neck, with the goal of a cleaner jawline. That use is outside the approved indication. A small prospective study of 12 patients reported that jowl injections produced improvement in most treated jowls, with swelling, bruising and pain as the common side effects. [2]

Kybella was developed by Kythera Biopharmaceuticals and approved by the US FDA on April 29, 2015; a generic became available in April 2021. [1] In September 2026 the FDA approved added label warnings about neuromuscular and other serious adverse events reported when it was injected outside the submental area. [3]

paras: The approved US use is reduction of moderate-to-severe fat below the chin. [1] Looksmaxxing and aesthetic practice discuss extending it to jowls and other neck areas, which is off-label. A review of male body contouring notes that men increasingly ask dermatologists and plastic surgeons for contouring procedures. [4]
Injected deoxycholic acid destroys fat cells (adipocytes) in the treated fat, and the body clears the contents over several months. [1]
In the 12-patient jowl study the reported adverse events were edema (9 patients), bruising (6), pain (5), induration (4), redness (3), numbness (2) and difficulty swallowing (1). [2]

Healio's report on the September 2026 FDA communication describes 129 adverse event cases from injections outside the submental region, including muscle or nerve injury such as facial paresis and paresthesia, reduced vision after use near the eye, and 117 cases of unresolved injection-site nodules or masses that lasted about five months on average. The FDA advises patients to seek care for signs of marginal mandibular nerve weakness, trouble swallowing or serious injection-site reactions. [3]

Kybella was developed by Kythera Biopharmaceuticals and approved by the FDA on April 29, 2015; a generic followed in April 2021. [1] In 2020 a dermatologic surgery group published an early protocol for jowl treatment. [2] In September 2026 the FDA approved additional label warnings about off-area use. [3]

A prospective study at a cosmetic practice between June 2016 and May 2017 injected deoxycholic acid into the jowls of 12 patients (11 women and 1 man; mild or moderate jowls). After the first session, of 24 jowls, 5 were rated as vastly improved, 15 as moderately improved and 4 as unchanged on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale; five jowls had a second session. The authors called it safe and effective for nonsurgical jowl reduction in this early experience. [2]

A phase 4 trial registered as NCT06783621, completed and enrolling 130 participants from January 2025, assessed patient satisfaction with overall face and neck appearance after combined treatment with onabotulinumtoxinA, Juvederm fillers, Kybella, CoolSculpting Elite and SkinMedica products. Because Kybella was one of several combined treatments, that registration does not isolate its effect. [5]

timeline.event: FDA approves Kybella on April 29 for submental fat. [1]
Dermatologic Surgery publishes a 12-patient jowl-reduction study. [2]
A generic version becomes available in the US. [1]
Phase 4 combined face and neck contouring study begins. [5]
FDA approves added label warnings about use outside the submental area. [3]
